tb-102-1.question:
Some drinks are stored in a refrigerator at 4 °C (Fig a).

When a canned drink and a drink in a plastic bottle are taken out of the refrigerator, which one feels colder? Why?

A They feel the same because their temperatures are the same.

B They feel the same because they have been placed in the same environment.

C The can feels colder than the plastic bottle because metal is a better conductor of heat.

D The plastic bottle feels colder than the can because plastic is a better insulator of heat.
tb-102-1.reasoning: The drinks should have about the same temperature when taken out. The can should feel colder as heat is conducted from our hands to the can more quickly than to the plastic bottle.

tb-102-2.question:
A pot of hot soup at 90 °C is placed in a closed space at room temperature. Which of the following statements is/are correct?

(1) Overall, the soup gains energy from the surroundings.

(2) The soup emits infra-red radiation.

(3) The soup stops emitting radiation when it reaches the room temperature.

A (1) only

B (2) only

C (1) and (3) only

D (2) and (3) only
tb-102-2.reasoning:
The soup has a temperature higher than room temperature. Overall, it should lose energy to the surroundings.

∴ (1) is incorrect.

A hot object emits infra-red radiation.

∴ (2) is correct.

An object at room temperature emits infra-red radiation, even though its temperature is the same as the surroundings.

∴ (3) is incorrect.

source.name: 102 Revision 2 Internal Energy, Heat and Transfer Processes.docx

tb-102-3.question:
An aluminium tray contains some cold salad. The tray is covered with a white paper lid and left in a space at room temperature (Fig b).

Which of the following about the heat transfer between the salad and the surroundings is/are correct?

(1) The aluminium tray reduces the heat transfer due to conduction.

(2) The aluminium tray reduces the heat transfer due to radiation.

(3) The paper lid reduces the heat transfer due to convection.

A (1) only

B (2) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-102-3.reasoning:
Aluminium is a good conductor of heat. It cannot reduce heat transfer due to conduction.

∴ (1) is incorrect.

The shiny aluminium tray is a poor absorber of radiation. It can reduce heat transfer due to radiation.

∴ (2) is correct.

The paper lid traps the cold air inside the tray and therefore reduces the heat transfer due to convection.

∴ (3) is correct.

It is known that one of the rods is a glass rod, one is a copper rod and one is an iron rod. Which of the following correctly matches the rods with the materials?

Option

Rod X

Rod Y

Rod Z

A

copper

iron

glass

B

iron

copper

glass

iron

glass

copper

glass

copper

tb-102-9.question:
Jerry places some ice cream scoops in a metal cup and a paper cup (Fig g and h).

(a) Explain, in terms of molecular motion, how energy is transferred by conduction between the paper cup and the ice cream scoops. (3 marks)

(b) Explain why the ice cream scoops melt more quickly in the metal cup than in the paper cup. (2 marks)
tb-102-9.answer:
(a) The molecules in the paper cup vibrate faster. 1A

They hit the slower neighbouring molecules in the ice cream scoops, making them vibrate more rapidly. 1A

Energy is transferred from the paper cup to the ice cream scoops through this process. 1A

(b) Metal is a better conductor of heat than paper. 1A

Heat is conducted more quickly to the ice cream scoops through the metal cup than through the paper cup. 1A

(b) Explain how the time needed for the ice to melt would be affected if the following changes are made separately.

(i) The glass boiling tube is replaced with a metal tube.

(ii) The lower part of the boiling tube is heated instead of the upper part. (6 marks)
tb-102-10.answer:
(a) Water is a poor conductor of heat. 1A

Therefore, heat is conducted slowly from the top part of the water to the ice at the bottom. 1A

(b) (i) The time would become shorter.
1A

Metal is a good conductor of heat. 1A

Heat can be conducted quickly to the ice through the metal tube. 1A

(ii) The time would become shorter.
1A

A convection current would be formed in the water. 1A

Therefore, all the water in the boiling tube would be heated up quickly. 1A

tb-102-12.question:
Figure l shows a model which demonstrates how a solar water heater works. When the model is put under sunlight, the water in the tube will be heated up and move back to the plastic bottle.

(a) Suggest an advantage of using a plate black in colour. Explain your answer. (2 marks)

(b) Suggest and explain whether the plate should be made of plastic or copper. (3 marks)

(c) Suggest an advantage of using a coiled tube in this model. Explain your answer. (2 marks)

(d) A student suggests that the water can be heated up more quickly if the plate is sealed in a transparent glass box. Comment on this suggestion. (3 marks)
tb-102-12.answer:
(a) A black surface is a good absorber of radiation. 1A

Therefore, a plate black in colour can effectively absorb sunlight and be heated up. 1A

(b) The plate should be made of copper.
1A

Copper is a better conductor of heat.
1A

Heat can be transferred from a copper plate to the water more quickly. 1A

(c) The coiled tube provides a large surface area. 1A

Heat can be conducted from the plate to the water quickly. 1A

(d) This suggestion is correct. 1A

The infra-red radiation emitted by the plate cannot pass through the glass. Therefore, the energy loss due to radiation is reduced. 1A

Warm air is trapped inside the box. Therefore, the energy loss due to convection is reduced. 1A

tb-102-14.question:
Read the following passage about a mug and answer the questions that follow.

A mug is a very common kind of cup. It is usually made of ceramic. The bottom surface of a mug is usually concave in shape (Fig n). This effectively reduces energy transfer between the mug and the table by conduction. The mug handle is also made of ceramic and has small contact areas with the body of the mug. Hence, the handle heats up unnoticeably even if the drink in the mug is very hot. With these features, most of the heat transfer is through the surface of the drink. To further reduce heat loss, you can choose a mug with a smaller opening or painted in a light colour. Of course, you can also cover your mug with a lid.

(a) How does a lid help reduce the heat transfer between the drink and the surroundings if the drink is (i) hot, (ii) cold? (3 marks)

(b) Suggest a colour for the lid so that it can best maintain the temperature of a drink. (1 mark)

(c) Explain why a small opening helps reduce energy loss. (1 mark)

(d) Consider a ceramic mug and a metal mug of the same size and shape. Which better maintains the temperature of a drink? Why? (2 marks)
tb-102-14.answer:
(a) (i) The lid reduces the heat transfer between the drink and the surroundings by convection 1A

and radiation. 1A

(ii) The lid reduces the heat transfer between the drink and the surroundings by radiation. 1A

(b) Silver 1A

(c) A smaller opening provides a smaller contact area between the drink and the air. Therefore, the energy loss due to conduction is reduced. 1A

(d) A ceramic mug maintains the temperature of a drink better. 1A

Ceramic is a better insulator of heat. Energy is transferred by conduction more slowly through a ceramic mug.
1A
